The REST module that serves `/ws/rest/v1` is `openmrs-module-webservices.rest`. Five production call sites there call `UserService.getUserByUuid`, ranked by how directly they depend on its result:

1. **`UserResource1_8.getByUniqueId`** (`omod/.../resource/openmrs1_8/UserResource1_8.java:207-211`): the user resource's GET-by-UUID. A changed return value (null vs. a user, or a different user) directly changes the HTTP response (404 vs. 200).
2. **`UserConverter1_8.getByUniqueId`** (`omod/.../converter/openmrs1_8/UserConverter1_8.java:34-37`): converts a UUID string into a `User` for any resource that references users. Affects every request that embeds a user reference.
3. **`ChangePasswordController1_8.changeOthersPassword`** (`omod/.../controller/openmrs1_8/ChangePasswordController1_8.java:67-85`): the admin password-change endpoint. A null return throws `NullPointerException`, so behaviour changes here affect password changes for other users.
4. **`ProviderSearchHandler1_9.search`** (`omod/.../search/openmrs1_9/ProviderSearchHandler1_9.java:52-64`): the provider `?user=<uuid>` search. A null return gives an empty result, so changes alter which providers are returned.
5. **`AlertRecipientResource2_0.setRecipientProperty`** (`omod/.../resource/openmrs2_0/AlertRecipientResource2_0.java:84-93`): resolves the recipient of an alert. A null return silently leaves the recipient unset.
